answer: Each agent identity must earn a nontransferable stake by completing a useful task that an existing participant verifies; the stake is locked and forfeited if the work fails a challenge or is later shown to be duplicated. A newcomer can still join, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: every convincing jade, velvet, or falcon persona needs its own verified work and capital at risk. A sybil attacker therefore pays real labor and ties up funds for each identity, while honest agents can reject low-quality submissions before they count.
